tasks.title: Locate the Fork Button
tasks.objective: Forking is a cornerstone of GitHub collaboration. It enables you to create a personal copy of a repository so you can experiment with changes without affecting the original project.
tasks.description: Go to the GitHub repository using the link below, locate the Fork button, and note where it's positioned.
tasks.outcome: By completing this task, you'll gain insight into how to initiate the process of forking a repository, a key step towards making personal contributions or testing changes independently. Understanding the forking mechanism is crucial for anyone looking to contribute to open source projects.
tasks.helpText: If you need help with this task, type 'help' in the comment box to get hints, but it will cost you 5 points from your total score.

tasks.title: Find the Issue Tracker
tasks.objective: The issue tracker is the hub for project discussions, bug reports, and feature requests. Your goal is to find the issue tracker within our GitHub repository.
tasks.description: Visit the GitHub repository in the link below and COUNT the number of open issues and provide that number in the comment box to complete the task.
tasks.outcome: This task will help you become familiar with how issues are reported, discussed, and tracked. Understanding the volume of discussions is crucial for grasping the project's activity level and areas that might need your contribution.
tasks.helpText: If you need help with this task, type "help" in the comment box to get hints, but it will cost you 5 points from your total score.
options: To list all contributors to the project
To track bug reports, feature requests, and project discussions
To store documentation and project guidelines
To manage pull requests and merges

hints.content: Make sure you click on the tab called "Issues" at the top of the page.
Make sure you count the right number of Open issues. Enter the number of open issues in the comment box.
